scope: Independent historical spelling and geographic context for the p215 third positions fragment. These sources are not a copy of the telegram and do not authenticate a unit, arrival, departure or November 1918 railway service.

sources.primary_observation: PDF page 7 contains a train timetable listing Ruttka, Zsolna, Teschen and Oderberg consecutively. PDF page 1 dates the issue to 8 July 1917. Title and timetable were visually checked.
sources.scope_limit: Supports the historic spellings and route adjacency in 1917; does not establish service or an actual movement in November 1918.

name_crosswalk.context: Békés county seat; Gyulai district seat.
name_crosswalk.cipher_qualification: The unchanged November square gives G4ULA. GYULA is the existing optional global Hungarian-Y interpretation of DD; the name does not justify a new observed-coordinate repair.

name_crosswalk.context: Arad county, Eleki district. Distinct from the separately listed Sikula.

name_crosswalk.normalization: Uppercase and proposed German cipher rendering ő → OE; the gazetteer itself prints ő, not OE.
name_crosswalk.cipher_qualification: The unchanged November square gives KIS9ENOE. KISJENOE uses the existing optional global J interpretation of GD and requires no additional observed-coordinate repair.

name_crosswalk.context: Arad county, Kisjenő district. The alphabetical entry on printed page 343 explicitly gives both.
name_crosswalk.normalization: Uppercase, ó → O and á → A.
name_crosswalk.cipher_qualification: Optional lexical hypothesis only. Beyond the main word layer it costs two observed-coordinate substitutions, one printed-mask fill and one added-loss fill; it fixes two additional letters, each with one observed half. The printed name does not eliminate this cost.

name_crosswalk.context: The same timetable sequence includes intervening Zsolna and following Oderberg.
name_crosswalk.cipher_qualification: Spelling and route context support the lexical chain. The first T of RUTTKA and final N of TESCHEN have no observed source half under either candidate geometry and remain explicitly lexical fills.
